lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.title: Guided practice: professional communication under time pressure

objective: Learners draft a clear, professional response to a provided fictional urgent workplace scenario within a short time limit, then compare it to a version they'd write without time pressure, to practice staying clear and professional even when rushed.
scenario: The learner reads a provided fictional urgent scenario (such as a same-day schedule conflict discovered at the last minute), drafts a response within a set short time limit, then afterward drafts an unhurried version of the same response and compares the two.
safetyNotes: The urgent scenario is fictional and provided with this lesson; the time limit is a practice constraint the learner sets for themselves, not a real deadline.

tasks.directions: Read the urgent scenario and, before timing yourself, note what makes it feel urgent.

prompts.text: Name what specifically makes this scenario time-sensitive, not just stressful.

tasks.directions: Set a five-minute timer and draft your response to the scenario within that limit.

prompts.text: Write your timed response, staying within the five-minute limit.
My timed response still states the key facts clearly, even though it was rushed.

tasks.directions: Now draft an unhurried version of the same response, without a time limit, and compare the two.

prompts.text: Write your unhurried version, then name what actually changed between the two, beyond just wording.

tasks.directions: Reflect on what stayed the same under pressure.

prompts.text: What part of your professional communication skills held up fine even under the time limit, and what part slipped?

remediation: If a learner's timed response omits a key fact or the core request entirely, reteach with a simple checklist to run through even under time pressure (what happened, what's needed, by when), then have the learner redo the timed draft using that checklist as a mental script.
extension: Have the learner repeat the exercise with an even shorter time limit for a different fictional scenario, and describe what they had to cut first when time ran shortest.
